newsitem.title: UK: British farmers' leader attacks EU green rate plan.
newsitem.headline: British farmers' leader attacks EU green rate plan.

text.p: A British farmers group has attacked EU plans to change the way subsidies are calculated.

Sir David Naish, president of the England and Wales National Farmers Union, has written to farm minister Douglas Hogg to express opposition to an EU commission proposal to cap the gap between frozen green rates and the currently applicable rate, the union said in a statement on Friday.

So-called green rates are used to convert EU subsidies, and institutional prices set for agricultural products under the EU's Common Agricultural Policy, from Ecus into the national currencies of the EU's member states.

The green rates used for calculating subsidies can be frozen to mitigate the income-cutting effects of rises in a currency, but now the EU wants to limit the difference between the rate used and the current rate.
The proposal has been opposed by Italy, Ireland and the United Kingdom.
"The Commission proposal would impose a limit from January 1 (1997) of seven percent of income lost in order to save the EU money," a spokesman for the Dutch presidency of the EU said on Thursday.
"But, these three countries say that the limit is unfair because it did not apply to countries which were compensated before that date," a Council official said later.
The Dutch presidency of the EU is hoping that the measures could be agreed next week.
